title: Speaking up and learning from mistakes
respondents: All employees, including bank staff and apprentices
summary: An anonymous March survey, six months after the September one: whether staff know how to raise a concern inside and outside the management chain, feel safe to, hold back and why, whether mistakes lead to learning, and bullying and harassment. About 7 minutes.
purpose: Shows whether staff who work alone in people's homes know how to raise a concern inside and outside the management chain, feel safe to do so, whether they hold back and why, and whether mistakes lead to learning or blame. It gives a six-monthly reading on the Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy, Incident Reporting, Investigation and Learning Policy and Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy targets measured in September, using the same wording, and measures bullying, harassment and sexual harassment, including from people we support and their households, as part of the duty to take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment.

timing.when: Once a year, opening on the second Monday of March for 3 weeks, after the equality monitoring survey closes; not in a year when the independent quality review staff questionnaire (SUR-CQC-002) runs in March

introduction:
{{organisation}} wants everyone to feel safe to speak up and to report mistakes. Please think about the last 12 months. It takes about 7 minutes, in paid working time. It is anonymous: we cannot see who answered, and our reports never show results for fewer than 5 people.

This survey cannot be used to raise a concern, because we cannot see who answered. To raise a concern, speak to any manager or our Speaking Up Lead, or use our Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy; you can also go straight to CQC or the council's adult safeguarding team, and Protect gives free, confidential advice.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your safety or someone else's, or need help now, phone the office or, out of hours, the On-call Manager (number in your staff handbook). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to make it safer to speak up and to learn from mistakes. Our legal reason is our legitimate interest in being a good employer and keeping people safe.

The survey is anonymous: we do not record your name, so your answers cannot be traced to you, and trying to identify someone is a disciplinary matter. CareFlow records only which branch an answer came from. Please do not write names. Only the HR Manager, the Registered Manager and the Nominated Individual look at individual answers. Our reports show results only for groups of 5 or more, and comments and branch results only for groups of 10 or more. If a comment describes someone at risk, we will act on it as far as we can.

We keep individual answers for 1 year after the survey closes, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. To ask about how we use information, contact the HR Manager or our Data Protection Officer. You can also complain to the Information Commission.

sections.title: Bullying and harassment
sections.introduction: These questions help us check that our steps to prevent harassment are working. You do not have to answer the questions about what has happened to you or what you have seen.

questions.text: In the last 12 months, has any of these happened to you at work? Choose all that apply.
questions.helpText: Bullying is offensive, frightening or insulting behaviour, or misuse of power, that upsets, humiliates or harms you. Harassment is unwanted behaviour linked to who you are, such as your race, religion, sex, sexuality, disability or age. Sexual harassment is unwanted sexual comments, messages, looks or touching.

howToRun: The HR Manager runs it. Use Send or schedule with everyone in your branches, repeating yearly, opening on the second Monday of March (after the equality monitoring survey closes), kept open 21 days; in a year when the independent quality review staff questionnaire (SUR-CQC-002) runs in March, skip this survey and that month's pulse. CareFlow records the branch of each anonymous answer, never the person. Agency workers are not sent it; they can use the speaking-up routes.

It is done in paid working time. Paper on request, in a sealed envelope to the HR Manager, who enters it alone with Record response, recorded as anonymous. No telephone completion: it could not be anonymous. Offer translated versions for staff whose first language is not English; never ask language. Set two reminders in Reminders and follow-up, one after 1 week and one after 2 weeks: on an anonymous survey CareFlow sends them to everyone who has not answered, with no personal link, and never to one person. CareFlow refuses an anonymous survey that would reach fewer than 5 people.

Who may open individual answers: the HR Manager, the Registered Manager and the Nominated Individual. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to the HR Manager, the Registered Manager and the Nominated Individual, and results to the same staff, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them.
actingOnResults: Comments are read each working day while the survey is open. Specific wrongdoing, abuse or a person at risk goes to the Registered Manager the same working day; as an anonymous concern the Nominated Individual is case owner and logs it under the Whistleblowing (Speaking Up) Policy, and if a person we support may be at risk the safeguarding lead acts the same day under the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure, as far as the information allows. An unreported incident described means the Registered Manager checks the incident log and repeats the reporting message at the next team meeting. Nobody tries to identify the writer: trying is a disciplinary matter.

How to count: positive means Strongly agree or Agree, Always or Usually, or Yes, leaving out Does not apply to me and Prefer not to say; for the routes question, the share choosing any option except the first. Targets (as in September): concern acted on 80%, not treated worse 80%, a route outside the line manager 90%, incidents 90%, know how to report harassment 90%, harassment handled fairly 80%. Never show a result for fewer than 5; flag 5 to 9 with no breakdown or comments; branch results and comments only for 10 or more. Small agencies combine branches or two years rather than lower the threshold.

Any target missed gets an action in the service improvement plan within 5 working days of the report. A branch with no concerns logged in 12 months and a speaking-up result below target goes to a Nominated Individual review within 10 working days. Fear for hours, job or visa in "What stopped you", or anyone seeing someone treated worse, means a Nominated Individual review of detriment checks and rota decisions, reported to the Directors. Any sexual or third-party harassment means the Registered Manager, with the HR Manager, reviews the harassment risk assessment within 1 month under the Sexual Safety Policy and the Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy. Not knowing what to do about abuse means safeguarding refreshers at team meetings and supervision.

Keep individual answers for 1 year after the survey closes under the Records Management and Retention Policy. For CQC, these results and actions evidence a speak-up and learning culture (Regulation 17(2)(e)).

regulatoryBasis.source: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 43B: protected disclosures, including disclosures about sexual harassment (subsection 1(da), from 6 April 2026)
Equality Act 2010, section 40A: an employer must take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of employees ("all" from 30 October 2026)
Equality Act 2010, section 40(1A) to (1C): an employer must not permit a third party to harass an employee, and is liable unless it took all reasonable steps to prevent it (from 30 October 2026)
Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 17(2)(e): seek and act on feedback from staff
